rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / THE STANDARD LIBRARY / CHAPTER 33

slides.title: Collections
slides.main: Specialized containers on top of built-ins: less code, fewer bugs.

slides.title: Counter
slides.main: A missing key gives zero, not an error; most_common returns the top at once.

body.text:
from collections import Counter

c = Counter("abracadabra")
print(c)
print(c.most_common(2))
print(c["z"], c["a"])
print(Counter("ab") + Counter("bc"))

slides.title: Counter in practice
slides.main: The counter handles the loop, dict and key check; only the task remains.

body.text:
from collections import Counter

text = "yes no yes no yes maybe"
print(Counter(text.split()).most_common(1))

def is_anagram(a, b):
    return Counter(a) == Counter(b)

print(is_anagram("listen", "silent"), is_anagram("cat", "tac "))
need = Counter("cat")
have = Counter("tackle")
print(not (need - have))

slides.title: defaultdict
slides.main: Even reading a missing key creates it; check with in or get.

body.text:
from collections import defaultdict

groups = defaultdict(list)
for w in ["apple", "banana", "apricot"]:
    groups[w[0]].append(w)
print(dict(groups))
counts = defaultdict(int)
for ch in "aabbb":
    counts[ch] += 1
print(dict(counts))
d = defaultdict(list)
print("x" in d, d["x"], "x" in d)

slides.title: deque
slides.main: Both ends are fast; maxlen makes the queue a window.

body.text:
from collections import deque

q = deque([1, 2, 3])
q.append(4)
q.appendleft(0)
print(q)
print(q.popleft(), q.pop(), q)
q.rotate(1)
print(q)
print(deque([1, 2, 3], maxlen=2))

slides.title: deque in practice
slides.main: Need a queue? deque. Need a stack? A list with append and pop is enough.

slides.title: namedtuple
slides.main: Best for records without logic: points, colors, table rows.

body.text:
from collections import namedtuple

Point = namedtuple("Point", ["x", "y"])
p = Point(3, 4)
print(p, p.x, p[1])
x, y = p
print(p._replace(x=10), p._asdict())
print(p == (3, 4))

slides.title: ChainMap and OrderedDict
slides.main: ChainMap glues dicts without copying; writes go to the first layer.

body.text:
from collections import ChainMap, OrderedDict

defaults = {"theme": "light", "font": 14}
user = {"font": 18}
cfg = ChainMap(user, defaults)
print(cfg["font"], cfg["theme"])
cfg["lang"] = "en"
print(user)

od = OrderedDict(a=1, b=2, c=3)
od.move_to_end("a")
print(list(od))

slides.title: heapq: the heap
slides.sub: The smallest is always at hand
slides.main: Need a max? Negate the numbers; priorities are tuples (priority, value).

body.text:
import heapq

h = []
for x in [5, 1, 4, 2]:
    heapq.heappush(h, x)
print(heapq.heappop(h), heapq.heappop(h), h[0])
tasks = []
heapq.heappush(tasks, (2, "mail"))
heapq.heappush(tasks, (1, "urgent"))
print(heapq.heappop(tasks))
print(heapq.nsmallest(2, [7, 3, 9, 1]), heapq.nlargest(2, [7, 3, 9, 1]))

slides.title: heapq in practice
slides.sub: Top k, merge, max via minus
slides.main: A heap isn't fully sorted: only the minimum at the start is guaranteed.

body.text:
import heapq

nums = [5, 1, 9, 3, 7, 8]
top3 = []
for x in nums:
    heapq.heappush(top3, x)
    if len(top3) > 3:
        heapq.heappop(top3)
print(sorted(top3, reverse=True))
print(list(heapq.merge([1, 4, 7], [2, 5], [3, 6])))
maxheap = [-x for x in nums]
heapq.heapify(maxheap)
print(-heapq.heappop(maxheap))

slides.title: bisect
slides.sub: Binary search in a sorted list
slides.main: Logarithmic search, but only if the data is already sorted.

body.text:
import bisect

nums = [10, 20, 20, 30]
print(bisect.bisect_left(nums, 20), bisect.bisect_right(nums, 20))
bisect.insort(nums, 25)
print(nums)

def grade(score, bounds=(60, 75, 90), names="DCBA"):
    return names[bisect.bisect(bounds, score)]

print(grade(55), grade(75), grade(95))

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: Subtracting counters, reading defaultdict, a "sorted" heap
slides.main: A list as a queue, bisect on unsorted data, comparing the incomparable: classics.

body.text:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import heapq

print(Counter("aab") - Counter("abb"))
d = defaultdict(list)
if d["none"]:
    pass
print(len(d))
h = [5, 1, 4]
heapq.heapify(h)
print(h == sorted(h), h[0])

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Before writing a loop, ask: is there a suitable container in the standard library?
